title: White-Label Case Study: Multi-Brand Architecture for 10+ Distinct Brands
topicCategory: 9. Staff / Senior System Design Interview Case Studies
subtopicTitle: White-Label Case Study: Multi-Brand Architecture for 10+ Distinct Brands
problemStatement:
Architecting a white-label frontend where a single codebase dynamically renders 10+ distinct brand identities with unique fonts, palettes, and density.

**Enterprise Importance**:
Crucial for B2B SaaS platforms (Shopify, Zendesk, Salesforce) that allow customers to brand their customer portals.
interviewTrap: Using `if (brand === 'BrandA')` conditionals inside component code. Brand logic must live exclusively in the token layer.

Components are 100% brand-agnostic. They only reference Semantic Tokens:

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Separate brand identity (tokens) completely from layout and component logic. Inject brand-specific semantic CSS variables at the root based on tenant configuration.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Design Token Layer: Primitives, semantic aliases, and component tokens established.
2. Component Architecture: Headless state and keyboard accessibility hooks implemented.
3. Styling & Cascade: Zero-runtime CSS variables and layer specificity managed.
4. Governance & Packaging: Tree-shaking, semantic versioning, and telemetry monitored.

complexity.time: O(1) CSS variable resolution at paint time / zero JavaScript runtime overhead
complexity.space: O(1) bundle footprint per imported component

edgeCasesHandled: Using `if (brand === 'BrandA')` conditionals inside component code. Brand logic must live exclusively in the token layer.
Keyboard focus traps, screen reader live regions, and WCAG 2.2 AA compliance.

verifiedRules: Tokens adhere to strict unidirectional dependency flow (Component -> Semantic -> Primitive).
All interactive primitives strictly adhere to keyboard navigation and screen reader accessibility invariants.
